macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as investors weigh U.S.-Iran tensions and oil price moves
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures rose after a bout of geopolitical stress, as markets stabilized alongside retreating oil prices. Reuters said investors were still weighing the impact of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran and the risk that energy costs could keep inflation elevated.

items.title: Global markets shaken by renewed Iran conflict; oil spikes and stocks retreat
items.summary: Market coverage from Yahoo Finance reported that the fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire was undermined, triggering a sharp jump in global oil prices and a broad pullback in stocks. The report also noted that August WTI crude closed up 4.37% and gasoline rose 5.06% in the prior session.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth outlook amid Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast, citing the economic fallout from the Iran war. The outlet said the IMF now expects global growth of 3% in 2026, with AI demand partly offsetting the energy shock.

items.title: Fed officials signal caution on inflation and future rate moves
items.summary: NBC News reported that Jerome Powell indicated further, smaller rate cuts while stressing the Fed is "not on any preset course." Financial Times also reported that some Fed officials saw a need for future rate rises to contain inflation, underscoring a more hawkish policy backdrop.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields steady after prior session spike
items.summary: CNBC reported that U.S. Treasury yields steadied after the previous session's jump, suggesting a partial stabilization in bond markets following the recent oil-driven inflation scare. Reuters also noted a broader rise in yields tied to renewed safe-haven and inflation concerns.

items.title: Asian and European equities mixed as sectors rotate on oil and tech moves
items.summary: Reuters reported that European shares rose in choppy trading, led by a rebound in technology stocks, while Asian shares also climbed as semiconductors recovered some of their losses. MarketScreener added that Australian shares wobbled as Fed caution offset oil-price optimism.

items.title: Japan’s Topix rises while Nikkei lags on tech weakness
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Japan's Topix advanced as oil prices fell, while the Nikkei was weighed down by technology stocks. The same market summary also highlighted a move higher in Samsung Electronics and gains in several European and commodity-linked assets.

items.title: U.S. labor data softer than expected, reinforcing growth concerns
items.summary: Financial Times reported that the U.S. economy undershot forecasts with 57,000 jobs added in June. That weaker labor backdrop adds to the macro focus on growth resilience and the Fed's next policy steps.

items.title: China inflation and producer prices show persistent cost pressures
items.summary: Reuters reported that China's producer prices rose for a fourth straight month and reached their highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also extended gains. The data suggested ongoing cost pressures for manufacturers amid broader supply-chain and energy concerns.

items.title: MarketScreener highlights several notable stock moves, led by Samsung Electronics
items.summary: MarketScreener's 24-hour market list showed Samsung Electronics among the most-mentioned movers, up 8.22%, with other gainers including Zalando, Bridgepoint, and Banco Santander. The same data showed modest moves in indices and commodities, including the DAX and WTI.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto markets slipped across major assets as risk appetite weakened
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 2.2% to roughly US$61,913, Ether dropped about 2.3% to US$1,733, XRP declined 3.9%, and Solana fell 5.2% over the last 24 hours. A separate market recap also described broader crypto weakness, with BTC and ETH lower and total market cap under pressure amid a risk-off backdrop.

items.title: SEC advances a major July regulatory overhaul agenda
items.summary: The SEC is preparing a substantial regulatory update this month with its anticipated “Regulation Crypto” agenda. The development suggests a major policy push that could affect trading, disclosures, and broader digital asset market rules.

items.title: India’s crypto policy remains uncertain as officials back tougher restrictions
items.summary: Reuters-reported government documents indicate Indian authorities are still pushing for tighter controls and possibly a blanket ban on digital assets. The Reserve Bank of India has reportedly continued to support a hardline approach favoring prohibition.

items.title: Coinbase legal leadership changes ahead of key crypto bill vote
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that Paul Grewal is leaving Coinbase’s legal leadership ahead of an important CLARITY vote. The timing makes the move notable because the bill could shape the U.S. crypto regulatory framework.

items.title: XRP gains attention as Ripple-linked banking use case expands
items.summary: crypto.news reported XRP price strength tied to SWIFT tapping Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The development highlights continued institutional interest in blockchain-based settlement infrastructure.

items.title: BNB Chain is building a new Layer 1 for agentic trading
items.summary: The Block reported that BNB Chain is developing a new Layer 1 aimed at agentic trading, with a target mainnet launch in 2027. The project points to continued infrastructure investment in blockchain-native automation and trading systems.

items.title: Binance Wallet adds access to Plume yield vaults tied to major fund managers
items.summary: The Block reported that Binance Wallet integrated Plume’s yield vault offering, giving users access to products linked to Invesco and Bitwise funds. The move reflects continued growth in tokenized and onchain yield products.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across multiple apps and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools and workplace automation. The move intensifies competition with other enterprise AI offerings from Anthropic and Meta.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release adds to the company’s recent push into more natural, multimodal AI interactions.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it more directly against OpenAI and Anthropic in the market for paid AI model access. The rollout signals Meta’s continued expansion of its model ecosystem.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched the Grok 4.5 model, describing it as its most intelligent release so far and emphasizing coding and agentic tasks. The launch adds to the rapid pace of high-end model releases across the industry.

items.title: Anthropic’s Claude gains regulatory relief
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude chatbot versions, ending a weekslong ban tied to cybersecurity concerns. The decision removes a major barrier for one of OpenAI’s top rivals.

items.title: New York publishers seek sanctions against OpenAI
items.summary: The New York Times and other newspapers asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in their copyright dispute, alleging the company withheld evidence about its ability to search for material used in AI training. The filing escalates one of the industry’s most closely watched legal fights.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for alleged violations of data protection rules. The penalty adds to growing regulatory scrutiny of consumer-facing AI chatbots.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip production
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to begin manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September as part of a broader effort to expand computing power. The company is also targeting a major increase in total compute capacity next year.

items.title: Nvidia probe in France nears conclusion
items.summary: France’s competition authority said its investigation into Nvidia is approaching an end. The development comes as regulators worldwide intensify scrutiny of AI infrastructure and chip market concentration.

items.title: AI industry focus shifts toward workplace agents and infrastructure
items.summary: Recent announcements show the industry moving quickly toward agentic AI, real-time voice systems, and tighter control over compute and chips. Legal and regulatory pressure remains a parallel trend, especially around copyright, privacy, and market power.
